description: FLAC (Free Lossless Audio Codec) decomposed. FLAC achieves ~50% lossless compression of PCM audio via linear prediction + Rice coding of the residual. The choice of prediction order, block size, and Rice parameters is content-adaptive per block. Byte-exact reconstruction of source PCM is the design constraint; everything is engineered around that.

sub_mechanisms.name: flac_block_structure
sub_mechanisms.definition: Audio divided into independent blocks (typically 4096 samples). Each block is encoded with its own prediction order, predictor type, residual coding parameters.
sub_mechanisms.why: Different content benefits from different predictor settings. Per-block adaptation lets each block use what works best for its content. Block size is encoder choice — smaller blocks adapt faster, larger blocks have lower header overhead.

sub_mechanisms.name: flac_fixed_predictors
sub_mechanisms.definition: 4 pre-defined linear predictors of order 0-4. Order 0: no prediction (just samples). Order 1: y[n] = y[n-1]. Order 2: y[n] = 2y[n-1] - y[n-2]. Etc. Encoder picks the order that minimises residual energy.
sub_mechanisms.why: Cheap to compute and decode. Captures simple temporal correlation. Order 0 for noise; order 4 for smooth low-frequency content. Sufficient for many content types; LPC is used for harder cases.

sub_mechanisms.name: flac_lpc_predictors
sub_mechanisms.definition: Up to order 32 linear predictor with explicitly-coded coefficients. Encoder fits LPC to the block, codes the coefficients + the residual.
sub_mechanisms.why: Higher order captures more complex correlation. The cost (sending coefficients) is per-block; with 4096-sample blocks, coefficient overhead is negligible. ~5-15% better compression than fixed predictors on complex content.

sub_mechanisms.name: flac_rice_coding
sub_mechanisms.definition: Residual coded with Rice (Golomb-Rice) codes. Each residual value v is split into v mod 2^k (k bits, fixed) and v >> k (unary). The parameter k is chosen per partition.
sub_mechanisms.why: Residuals after good prediction are Laplacian-distributed (peaked at zero, exponential tails). Rice codes are near-optimal for this distribution. Choosing k per partition lets the encoder match the local residual variance.

sub_mechanisms.name: flac_rice_partition
sub_mechanisms.definition: Residuals are divided into partitions; Rice parameter k is chosen separately per partition. Partition size is signalled in the header.
sub_mechanisms.why: Residual variance can change within a block (e.g., loud section vs quiet section). Per-partition k adapts to local variance without breaking the block structure. ~2-5% additional saving over single-k coding.

sub_mechanisms.name: flac_channel_decorrelation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Stereo decorrelation: encoder can store L/R, M/S, L/S (L + side), or R/S — picking whichever produces the lower entropy.
sub_mechanisms.why: Stereo content typically has correlated L and R; storing M and S is more compressible. The choice is per-block; some blocks have nearly-correlated channels (M/S wins), others have independent channels (L/R wins). Encoder picks the best per block.

sub_mechanisms.name: flac_frame_header
sub_mechanisms.definition: Each frame: sync code + block size + sample rate + channel assignment + bit depth + CRC. Self-synchronising for stream resync.
sub_mechanisms.why: Same role as MP3's sync header. Allows mid-stream tuning, error recovery, frame-level seeking. The CRC catches transmission errors.

sub_mechanisms.name: flac_metadata_blocks
sub_mechanisms.definition: FLAC streams begin with metadata blocks (typed): STREAMINFO (mandatory: stream-level parameters), VORBIS_COMMENT (tags), PICTURE (album art), APPLICATION (custom).
sub_mechanisms.why: Self-describing format. Decoders/players parse the metadata to know what they're dealing with before processing audio. The block structure lets new metadata types be added without breaking older parsers.

sub_mechanisms.name: flac_predictability_constraint
sub_mechanisms.definition: Encoder ensures the bitstream is deterministically decodable on any conforming decoder — bit-exact reconstruction of PCM samples.
sub_mechanisms.why: Lossless requires this. The spec defines the predictor types, Rice coding, and reconstruction order exactly; deviation produces non-decodable streams. The integer arithmetic everywhere ensures byte-exactness across platforms.

sub_mechanisms.name: flac_subset_streams
sub_mechanisms.definition: FLAC defines a 'subset' constraint: certain combinations of parameters (max block size, max LPC order, max sample rate) are guaranteed decodable by minimal decoders.
sub_mechanisms.why: Decoder implementers can target a known subset and not worry about extreme parameter combinations. Subset streams are guaranteed to decode on any conformant subset decoder; full FLAC may need more elaborate decoders.

sub_mechanisms.name: flac_compression_level
sub_mechanisms.definition: Encoder presets 0-8 (0 = fastest, 8 = best compression). Higher levels search more block sizes, predictor types, Rice parameters.
sub_mechanisms.why: Same trade as x264 presets: more search = better compression at higher encode cost. Decoder cost is unaffected (decode complexity is fixed by the format). Encoder typically defaults to level 5.

sub_mechanisms.name: flac_seek_table
sub_mechanisms.definition: Optional metadata block listing the byte offsets of selected sample positions. Players use it for fast seeking without scanning.
sub_mechanisms.why: Without it, seeking requires parsing frames sequentially. The seek table is small (a few bytes per checkpoint) and makes random access fast — important for streaming and editing.

derivation_rules.name: lossless_compression_bounded_by_signal_entropy
then: compression ratio is bounded by Shannon entropy
derivation_rules.why: Lossless coding cannot beat Shannon's source-coding theorem. FLAC's ~50% compression reflects audio's ~50% redundancy. Beating this would require finding more structure in the signal; current FLAC is near the entropy bound for typical audio.

derivation_rules.name: rice_codes_near_optimal_for_laplacian_residuals
if: the residual distribution is Laplacian (peaked at zero, exponential tails)
derivation_rules.why: Rice's mathematical form matches the Laplacian distribution. The parameter k controls how many bits to spend on the body vs the tail. For correctly-chosen k, Rice's overhead vs the entropy bound is small. Common across lossless audio codecs (FLAC, ALAC, WavPack).

derivation_rules.name: per_block_adaptation_matches_local_statistics
if: different blocks have different signal statistics
then: per-block parameter selection beats fixed parameters
derivation_rules.why: Audio's statistics vary — quiet sections vs loud, voiced vs unvoiced, music vs silence. Per-block prediction order, predictor type, partition size, Rice parameter all matter. Fixed parameters waste bits on blocks where they don't fit.

derivation_rules.name: fixed_predictors_for_simple_content_lpc_for_complex
then: fixed predictors beat LPC at lower encode cost
derivation_rules.why: LPC coefficient overhead is per-block; if a fixed predictor already captures most of the correlation, LPC's overhead exceeds its gain. Encoder picks LPC only when its compression gain exceeds the coefficient cost. Simple content → fixed predictors.

derivation_rules.name: channel_decorrelation_per_block_finds_optimum
if: L and R have variable correlation across blocks
then: per-block decorrelation choice finds the optimum
derivation_rules.why: Sometimes M/S compresses better; sometimes L/R; sometimes one channel + the side. Per-block selection picks whichever produces the lowest entropy. Same insight as AAC's per-band M/S vs L/R selection.
